title: `Find in Files` can't find text inside builtin scripts (regression?)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.dev5.mono.official [a8643700c]

### System information

Windows 10 - Foward+ - Dedicated NVIDIA GeForce 1070

### Issue description

Both `Find in Files (Ctrl+Shift+F)` and `Replace in Files (Ctrl+Shift+R)` can't find the text inside built-in scripts. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a33569c-5edf-45d5-9b78-218fbcbc70bf

This can lead to ghost prints inside debug builtin script files that you can't find later.

This looks like a regression from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/74145

But I tried Godot 4.5, 4.3, 4.2 and 4.1 and it didn't work on any of them.
So I think this issue got a regression even before the release and never even made it to stable.

---

This is most likely because of the extension **Filter**. They only include `.gd, .cs and .gdshader`. 
So the .tscn files are never included in the search, and that PR code is never really used.

I think adding a .tscn filter option (with default off) should help solve this and avoid tanking the search performance for most normal search use cases.

### Steps to reproduce

**Steps:** 
- Create a builtin script that has a line with `print("Ghost print")` inside.
- Ctrl+Shift+F (Find in Files) and search for "Ghost print"

**Result:** Nothing found
**Expected:** Found the text inside the builtin script

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[ghost_print_search.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27034217/ghost_print_search.zip)
